pages.title: Chat
pages._note: Custom page: a streaming chat thread is genuinely custom — SSE token/tool-call consumption with a live assistant bubble, a conversation archive lifecycle driven by Hermiq's payload-marker soft delete, per-message feedback, and an agent-selector empty state are not expressible via the built-in index/detail/dashboard page types (agent-engine-port). Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: Agents
pages._note: Custom page: the agent catalog needs bespoke behaviour (createObjectStore agents in the hermiq register + schedule-attached/last-run derivation + create modal) that the built-in index page type cannot express. Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: Agent
pages._note: Custom page: agent detail combines the createObjectStore agent object, schedule attach/edit (createObjectStore), the thin Run-now endpoint, and run history — not expressible via the built-in detail page type.

pages.title: Approvals
pages._note: Custom page: the reviewer inbox is reviewer-scoped (not owner-scoped OR objects) with guarded approve/deny actions and the org kill-switch — not expressible via the built-in index page type. Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: Memory
pages._note: Custom page: agent memory combines the createObjectStore agent collection (picker) with tenant-scoped Memory/Session objects, a char-budget bar, the consolidation nudge + manual consolidate, and OR-search recall — not expressible via the built-in index/detail page types. Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: Sessions
pages._note: Custom page: conversation sessions are the OpenRegister agents resource (picker) plus tenant-scoped Session/SessionTurn objects served agent-scoped (/agents/{id}/sessions, /recall), not the generic objects/{register}/{schema} path, so the built-in index page type cannot express it. Split from Memory so chats are their own surface.

pages.title: Skills
pages._note: Custom page: the skills catalog imports/exports agentskills.io packages (lossless SkillSerializer round-trip) and installs a skill onto an agent (installedOn association) — not expressible via the built-in index/detail page types. Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: AI features
pages._note: Custom page: the AI-feature governance register drives action-auth-gated DPO-acknowledgement + a declarative OpenRegister enable/disable lifecycle (enable is blocked until the DPO acknowledges) — governance actions not expressible via the built-in index/detail page types. Standard nav page — not a dashboard.

pages.title: Analytics
pages._note: Dashboard page: run analytics as two custom widgets (KPIs + status/per-agent breakdown) over the computed /api/analytics endpoint. Runs are not OR-schema objects, so these are custom kind:widget components, not declarative stats-block dataSources.

pages.title: Tenant ops
pages._note: Custom page: per-org quota usage + EU AI Act audit export (download) over OpenRegister objects/AuditTrail, capability-gated to org owners/admins — not expressible via the built-in index/dashboard page types. Standard nav page.

pages.title: MCP tools
pages._note: Custom page: catalogue of MCP tools available to agents, read from Hermiq's facade-backed /api/agents/tools endpoint (not register/schema objects), so the built-in index page type cannot express it. Read-only nav page.

pages.title: Compliance
pages._note: Custom page: per-framework compliance-control coverage + gap list computed live from existing governance data (never a hand-ticked field), plus an auditor's-pack export — not expressible via the built-in index/dashboard page types. Standard nav page, action-auth-gated.

steps.title: Welcome to Hermiq
steps.body: Hermiq runs autonomous agents against a local LLM. Point it at your Ollama host and test the connection once — agents can't run without a reachable model.

steps.title: Test connection
steps.body: Probe the endpoint and confirm Hermiq can reach your models. The first model discovered becomes the default.

steps.title: Welcome to Hermiq
steps.body: Let's take a quick tour. Hermiq lets you build autonomous AI agents, give them skills and tools, and run them on a schedule.
Agents are the heart of Hermiq. Open Agents to see them and define your own.

steps.title: Your agent catalog
steps.body: This is where your agents live. Use New to create one — give it a prompt, pick a model, and add optional tools and skills.
Skills give agents new abilities. Browse the Skills catalog to see what you can add.
MCP tools connect your agents to external systems over the Model Context Protocol.
steps.task: Click MCP tools in the menu

steps.title: You're all set
steps.body: That's the tour. Open Settings any time to re-run this walkthrough or the setup wizard.
